Chapter 6: Becoming a “Fred” in Any Role
You know, it’s really easy to look at someone like the mail carrier and think, “Well, that’s just who he is. I could never be like that.” But here’s the thing—the qualities that set Fred apart? They’re not reserved for just a few special people.
They’re actually choices—habits of mind and heart that anyone can develop, no matter your job, your background, or your personality.
Let me paint you a picture. Imagine a hospital orderly, quietly moving through the halls. Most folks barely notice them. The work can be repetitive, the hours are long, and let’s be honest, recognition is pretty rare. But this particular orderly decides to treat every single patient with the same genuine care that Fred brought to his mail route.
Instead of rushing through tasks, they pause to ask how someone’s feeling, offer a comforting word, or maybe just adjust a pillow for a little extra comfort. Over time, patients start asking for this orderly by name. The whole atmosphere on the ward begins to shift. Nurses and doctors notice, and even the most anxious patients seem a little more at ease.
That’s when you realize—being a “Fred” isn’t about the job itself. It’s about how you choose to do it. Most people don’t realize just how much power they have to shape their environment. But those who do—like that orderly—become a quiet force for good.
They don’t wait for permission or for someone to give them a pat on the back. They just choose to care, to notice, and to take action.
A lot of us fall into the trap of thinking only certain roles let you have this kind of impact. But here’s something to pay attention to: every job, no matter how humble, gives you chances to make a difference.
It’s not about having special skills or tons of resources. It’s about bringing intention and heart to whatever you do.
The mail carrier’s story reminds us—anyone can be a “Fred.” It’s a choice you make, moment by moment, to bring your best self to your work and your relationships. And when you do, not only do you improve the lives of those around you—you’ll also discover a deeper sense of meaning and satisfaction in your own life.
